summary.headline: PNB Housing Q2 FY27 disbursements rose 60% YoY to INR 9,609 crore and spread widened to 2.43%, aided by a one-off; loan book up 19% YoY to INR 95,079 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was a strong quarter: disbursements of INR 9,609 crore (+60% YoY, including INR 838 crore pool buyout) and retail disbursements at an all-time high of INR 9,250 crore (+54%). Profit after tax rose 6% YoY to INR 617 crore, with ROA of 2.53% and ROE of 12.33%, both flattered by a one-off prepayment recovery; management says normalised ROA is about 2.4%. GNPA improved to 0.91% from 0.95% in Q1, and a INR 75 crore write-off recovery produced negative credit cost of 19 bps. The company was upgraded to AAA by CRISIL, taking all four domestic agencies to AAA, and management expects a phased benefit to borrowing costs.

segments.name: Affordable (Roshni)
segments.commentary: Disbursements INR 1,149 crore, +40% YoY; affordable book up 45% YoY. Management says Roshni yield is flat while prime/emerging-sourced affordable business dilutes overall yield by 10-12 bps.

segments.name: Emerging markets
segments.commentary: Disbursements INR 2,882 crore, +36% YoY; book up 22% YoY. Affordable plus emerging together are 41% of retail book, targeted at 45% by end-FY27.

segments.name: Prime
segments.commentary: Disbursements INR 4,380 crore, +44% YoY. Prime disbursement mix in Q2 was about 60% self-employed and 40% salaried.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Disbursements INR 360 crore vs INR 215 crore in Q1; corporate book INR 689 crore.

guidance_outlook: Loan book growth guidance of 18-20% for FY27 maintained; management says current 19% should improve.
Expect spread and NIM to improve further as incremental yield (9.64%) exceeds book yield and rates rise; leverage increase will partly offset NIM.
Expected cost of borrowing rise of 9-10 bps from the 25 bps repo hike, rising to 12-15 bps by end-Q4; proposed lending rate hikes of 10-15 bps retail and 15-20 bps corporate effective 1 November.
Normalised ROA guidance of about 2.4% maintained.
Credit cost expected to settle at about 10-12 bps once recoveries stop.
FY28 strategy being prepared in Q3; intent is not to degrow. Target of INR 3,000 crore construction finance book this year.
capex_capacity: Distribution network of 404 branches as of 30 September 2026: 234 Roshni affordable, 88 emerging market and 81 prime branches.
Pool buyout of INR 986 crore completed in H1 FY27 against an annual plan of about INR 2,000 crore; combination of home loan and LAP.
Micro Housing business launched in Q2, INR 71 crore disbursed; INR 107 crore disbursed under Emerging Developer Finance in H1.
Investments this year mainly in affordable branches and manpower; Opex up 20% YoY.
AI: Voice AI POC for Bucket X collections completed; next two quarters focus on moving POCs to production.
demand_pricing: Management sees no demand slowdown after the 25 bps repo hike; logins, sanctions and disbursements unchanged as of late October.
Peers have passed on 15-20 bps; PNB plans 10-15 bps on retail and 15-20 bps on corporate from 1 November.
Competition is strongest in metro and state-capital prime/emerging branches; Roshni in Tier 3-4 remains the strategic focus.
Management avoids head-to-head pricing with PSU banks in salaried prime home loans, focusing on self-employed and LAP.
Insurance commission regulation under discussion; mitigation via DA income, processing fees and cost control. Management expects premium to fall 30-40% if implemented.
Q3 and Q4 are seasonally stronger (festive season).

qa_highlights.question: What is the one-off charge from the legacy corporate account and how is it accounted for?
qa_highlights.answer: Overdue charges and overdue interest collected on closure of one legacy corporate account. Accounted for on receipt basis, so booked in Q2 as a one-off; it lifted yield, spread and NIM by roughly 12-17 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sensitivity of cost of borrowing and margins to a 50 bps repo hike?
qa_highlights.answer: A 25 bps hike adds 9-10 bps to cost of borrowing, rising to 12-15 bps by end-Q4; a 50 bps hike would add about 20 bps, with 20-30 bps passed on to the portfolio.

qa_highlights.question: Is rate-hike-driven demand softening, and how are competitors pricing?
qa_highlights.answer: No change in momentum observed so far. Most HFCs have raised rates by 15-20 bps; pass-through expected at 15-20 bps.

qa_highlights.question: What is the normalised credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: About 11 bps excluding the INR 75 crore recovery; management expects 10-12 bps once recoveries stop.

qa_highlights.question: Why are non-housing loans rising in the mix and how long will this continue?
qa_highlights.answer: About 60% of incremental disbursements (excluding pool buyout) are housing and about 40-48% non-housing, managed within PBC norms; pool sell-down of non-housing assets is being explored.

qa_highlights.question: Why is 30+ DPD on the 24-month vintage up from about 0.2% to 0.4%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not significant, 90+ DPD is stable and bounce rates have improved; the company will deep-dive the trend.

risks_watch: Rate pass-through: borrowing costs are rising with the repo hike, and pass-through may fall short of the 15-20 bps assumed.
Asset quality in affordable LAP and the 30+ DPD trend on newer vintages (0.2% to 0.4% QoQ).
Corporate written-off pool of about INR 650 crore from two accounts declared fraud, still under recovery; retail written-off pool about INR 320 crore.
Q2 ROA and spread include one-offs; normalised spread is 2.24% and normalised NIM about 3.49%.
Insurance commission regulatory change could hit fee income; outcome still under discussion.
Rising leverage will offset part of the NIM benefit; repricing of old borrowings expected to be gradual, with measurable benefit next year.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and demand, with management saying the rate hike has not dented sourcing. Cautious on credit rating benefits, which will take time, and on margin upside, which management frames as likely but not quantified. Evasive on the regulatory insurance-commission question, which it called still in discussion.

growth.why: Loan book growth guidance of 18-20% for FY27 held (current 19%, management says it should improve), backed by Q2 disbursements up 60% YoY to INR 9,609 crore and a INR 3,000 crore construction finance target, with 404 branches and new affordable branches/manpower investment; no hard capacity numbers given for the growth, and FY28 strategy is still being prepared.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Incremental yield 9.64% exceeds book yield and incremental cost of borrowing is 7.26%, but normalised spread is 2.24% and NIM about 3.49% ex one-off, with leverage and repricing of old borrowings offsetting part of the gain.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 404 branches (234 Roshni, 88 emerging, 81 prime) and new affordable branches/manpower are being added, but no branch count target or capacity numbers were given for the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Loan book up 19% YoY to INR 95,079 crore vs 18-20% FY27 guidance held, retail disbursements +54% YoY to INR 9,250 crore, and Q3-Q4 seasonally stronger with no demand slowdown after the 25 bps repo hike.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is not discussed and no utilisation figure was given; investment is opex-led (affordable branches, manpower, opex up 20% YoY to INR 260 crore), so no new plant or capex announcement is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Loan book growth guidance of 18-20% held with current 19% that management says should improve, but ROA guidance of normalised 2.4% was only maintained, not raised.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Pass-through of 9-10 bps cost-of-borrowing increase may fall short of the 15-20 bps lending hikes assumed, 30+ DPD on 24-month vintage rose 0.2% to 0.4%, and insurance commission regulation could cut premium 30-40% if implemented.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Micro Housing launched in Q2 with INR 71 crore disbursed and Emerging Developer Finance at INR 107 crore in H1; construction finance book target of INR 3,000 crore this year.

rows.label: Lending rate hikes of 10-15 bps retail, 15-20 bps corporate
rows.why: Peers passed on 15-20 bps and PNB plans 10-15 bps retail and 15-20 bps corporate from 1 November, offsetting the 9-10 bps rise in borrowing cost, rising to 12-15 bps by end-Q4.

rows.label: Pool buyout run-rate against annual plan
rows.why: INR 986 crore pool buyout completed in H1 against an annual plan of about INR 2,000 crore, implying roughly INR 1,000 crore more would be needed in H2 if the plan is met.

rows.label: AAA rating from all four domestic agencies
rows.why: CRISIL upgrade takes all four agencies to AAA; management expects a phased benefit to borrowing costs, but repricing of old borrowings is gradual with measurable benefit next year.
